title: drop on the iterator of an empty Range can make it non-empty: it then yields elements outside the range, indexWhere returns a position and segmentLength walks 2^32 elements
oracle: an iterator of an empty range stays empty after drop; BigInt model
generator: wave4/harness/collections3/RangeDiff.scala: empty ranges produced directly and by take(0), slice and takeRight(0) near the Int bounds, then iterator.drop / indexWhere(p, from) / segmentLength(p, from)
signature: Range | .slice(#,#) | it.hasNext | val -> val; HANG at segmentLength
detail: RangeIterator.drop (src/library/scala/collection/immutable/Range.scala, class RangeIterator) sets _hasNext from a comparison of the new position with lastElement and never consults whether the iterator was already exhausted or initially empty. For an empty range lastElement is not an element; for (Int.MinValue until Int.MinValue) it is Int.MaxValue after wrapping, so drop(1) turns hasNext to true and the iterator yields -2147483647, -2147483646 and so on for 2^32 elements. (4 until Int.MaxValue by -1) and (Int.MaxValue until Int.MaxValue by -1) behave the same. The inherited indexWhere(p, from) and segmentLength(p, from) use iterator.drop(from), so on such an empty range indexWhere(_ => true, 1) returns 1 and segmentLength(_ => true, 1) runs through the 2^32 elements (about 3 s, then returns -1 after its counter wraps; the reproduction waits 1 s). The integration build contains the LI7 change to this method and still fails. Empty ranges with a start at a bound, or with a step pointing away from the end, are needed.
fix_sketch: In drop, do nothing when !_hasNext. No compatibility cost.
prior: LI7 (retronym/scala#558): same method, overflow of the position for a non-empty range; this is the empty-range case that fix leaves
